flawed_step: The claim that termination holds for any choice of augmenting paths fails for irrational capacities: an adversarial path choice can make the bottlenecks shrink geometrically forever.
counterexample: r=(sqrt5-1)/2, so r^2=1-r. Vertices s,t,a1,b1,a2,b2,a3,b3. Special arcs e1=a1->b1 (capacity 1), e2=a2->b2 (capacity r), e3=a3->b3 (capacity 1). All other arcs have capacity 10: s->v and v->t for every inner v, and ai->aj, bi->bj for i!=j. State = forward residuals (x1,x2,x3) of (e1,e2,e3). Step 0: s-a3-b3-t, bottleneck 1, giving (1,r,0). Step 1: s-a2-b2-b3-a3-t (e2+,e3-), bottleneck r, giving A_0=(1,0,r). From A_n=(r^n,0,r^{n+1}) with flows (1-r^n,r,1-r^{n+1}): (b) s-a1-b1-b2-a2-a3-b3-t (e1+,e2-,e3+), bottleneck r^{n+1}, giving (r^{n+2},r^{n+1},0); (c) s-a2-b2-b3-a3-t (e2+,e3-), bottleneck min(r^{n+1},1)=r^{n+1}, giving (r^{n+2},0,r^{n+1}); (d) s-a3-b3-b2-a2-a1-b1-t (e3+,e2-,e1+), bottleneck min(r^{n+1},r,r^{n+2})=r^{n+2}, giving (0,r^{n+2},r^{n+3}); (e) s-a2-b2-b1-a1-t (e2+,e1-), bottleneck min(r^{n+2},1)=r^{n+2}, giving A_{n+2}. The cycle repeats forever. The 10-capacity arcs are used only forwards, and the total pushed is 1+r+2/r (about 4.854), which is below 10, so they never limit a bottleneck. Every step is legal, so the method never terminates. The flow value tends to about 4.854, while the maximum flow is at least 30.
assessment_summary: Zwick-style counterexample with capacities 1, r, 1 where r is the inverse golden ratio. An explicit, checked cycle of four augmentations takes state A_n to A_{n+2}, so augmenting paths exist forever and Ford-Fulkerson never terminates. The flow value converges to about 4.854, well below the maximum of at least 30. The statement is false.
